critique: Top MoA is Actin disruptors, runner-up Eg5 inhibitors. Mechanism: actin-driven condensation and altered actin polymerization cause actin aggregation, membrane instability, and cytokinesis failure. F-actin grows as small granules and clusters into large aggregates. Consequently, cell morphology shows actin at the rim as bright actin pores, clustered actin, and labile cortex, with cell shrinkage and peripheral condensation, and beta-tubulin compacted. Beta-tubulin shows punctate z=+29 classes and good clustering, with z=+29 classes compacted ±45-50% into 825-well-class cytotectonic breast region. Strong staining bands reveal actin texture, retraction, and cell shrinkage. F-actin concentrates in the perinuclear region as actin-rich aggregates, actin bundles, actin stress fibers, and perinuclear actin foci, with possible altered/increased actin staining. Time-lapse or phalloidin imaging shows actin aggregates colocalized with phalloidin. DNA/nuclei show actin pore-induced membrane changes, nuclear condensation, nuclear shrinkage, and fragmented DNA, with cell-cycle progression arrested in G2, G2/M, G2/S, and multinucleated cells arising from cytokinesis failure, mitotic pause/arrest from secondary failure of mitotic spindle checkpoints, and mitotic catastrophe. Combination with F-actin probes at a late time point shows that in the membrane, disrupted F-actin exhibits specific loss of microtubule stability and severe cell-cycle arrest, with severe loss of cell proliferation. These features are supported by beta-actin aggregates, colocalization of actin secretion, cell shrinkage concentrated in the network, high-density actin texture and actin proteins, altered actin distribution, punctate actin aggregates, and perinuclear actin foci. Core-peripheral actin staining appears as strong actin spots, and actin-rich spots show partial fragmentation. Bundled actin shows a bright cloudy band at the poles with enriched perinuclear staining and active actin bundles.

critique: Approving SAR Phase 1 by a zipper model where each IF event has a COO that is solidified in destabilization and atrophied in apoptosis (IF5) is not justified at any stated strength. IF4's COO gating is confounded by selection, and the order effect is sesnsitive to reclassifications. Among several candidates, only cadA/BsaI has randomized/COU-supported evidence for cycle counting and adequacy. The remaining monies require purposeful design. No grading of raters by rhoe or rhoematopoietic can substitute for disjoint replication that changes only one SAR factor.

critique: Clean on the conceded grounds - every test compound and the test article's own NSA pass the mtDNA fluorescence-quench test that C2 broke, so the genotoxicity was C2-specific and the panel shows no general dye-artifact; TK advice is appropriately restrained (assay-driven cargo, no recommendation to strip the centrifuge step despite TK's incentive) and the report-layer error is correctly treated as a provenance failure pending backbone-anchored re-derivation rather than a verdict on the assay. Remaining gaps: (1) rescue is still single-reader and unquantified - 'establish first' was planned against a same-session positive control, but no auditable recovery value or control result for the actual C1/C2 rescue is on file, so 5/6 remains an unquantified microscopy read; syndrome-search scores-based 5/6 is defensible given the fixed CI rule, but the empirical anchor the roA advance prescribed is a manual read. (2) Both inferential quantities - a panel of four scored with a-posteriori-singleton caution and a recovery read from the near-collapsed preparation - carry no uncertainty characterisation, and the go decision rests on 'stronger bands across the tracked radionucleotide window' from a precipitated, source-less report; the fall-through dATP-window trap is conceded sympathetically in the fall-through, but the fact that the conceding actor's own body text still carries an unresolved internal inconsistency (a second named matter in his own message asserts the labels as a flat 0/6, corrected only by cross-reference to his own fall-through) shows the same unaudited-number fragility now lives inside the validation layer. (3) The prior-structure risk is fully conceded as 'pointed at the conclusion'/'could have grown legs' for ablations and priors alike, yet the claim still rests that pilots 'put this sequence gate to work'; because the presumption was admittedly pointed when first read, panel selection bias (drop-recovery results surfacing in the unlabeled report) could equally have seeded all four tracked candidates, and a targeted confirmation experiment on a preparation that scored normally, independent of the DN-treated collapse/recovery contrast, is the proportionate, falsifiable next test the report explicitly reserves. (4) Dosage: what exists is 'the very next step' plus 'derive the thresholds' - there is no quantitative recovery mapping, so upside exists but remains conditional on writing it down; until then the remedy is unvalidated. None of this yet justifies abandoning the approach; it means the claim should stay gated to the pre-registered early, near-dilution window, classed as promising-but-unconfirmed rather than established.

critique: Do not approve. The Microtubule stabilizers call at 0.6 rests mainly on the atlas (e5, e9), but that vote is only 2/4 wells and the decisive similarity is confined to the single 3 µM well (0.61); the 0.3-1 µM wells are near-noise (0.19-0.27) and vote for other classes, so they do not independently support the top class. The non-atlas evidence does not favour stabilizers over the runner-ups: tub_mean falls monotonically with dose (e14, rho=-1.0; 3 µM tub_mean z=-5.1), the opposite of the increased/bundled tubulin signal expected for stabilizers, and the microscopist explicitly saw no microtubule bundling or loss at 3 µM (e4) and an essentially DMSO-like, intact filamentous tubulin picture at 1 µM (e13). frac_mitotic_like is not dose-dependent (e10, rho=-0.20) and drops at 3 µM, arguing against a clean mitotic-arrest mechanism. The extreme phenotype (nuc_solidity z=-36, e2/e15) appears abruptly only at the single highest-dose well, with cell loss (e12), smaller fragmented nuclei and cortical actin brightening; that high-dose picture is equally compatible with Aurora kinase inhibitors / Eg5 inhibitors-type segregation failure or generic cytotoxic fragmentation, as the microscopist noted (e4), and does not discriminate the top class. With every dose represented by one well and no replicate, the stated 0.6 is over-confident: stabilizers are at best a plurality, not more likely than all alternatives combined.
requested_experiment: Acquire one well at dose index 6 (1.0 µM), replicate 2 - the highest sub-catastrophic dose, where the leading hypotheses make opposite, testable predictions before the 3 µM fragmentation/cell-loss confound. If replicate 2 reproduces tubulin loss without bundling/mitotic enrichment, the stabilizer call should fall toward Microtubule destabilizers or a mitotic-segregation class; if it shows bundling with mitotic enrichment, the top call gains its first non-atlas support. This single replicate directly tests the weak transition-dose effect on which discrimination depends.

critique: Approach is methodical (multi-dose design, hypothesis tracking, dose-response checks) but the conclusion is not well supported. The NSC/protocol call is unanimous for Eg5 inhibitors (4/4 wells, 10/10 neighbours), yet the direct phenotypic evidence points at least as strongly the other way: the microscopist saw large spread cells with multilobed/grape-like micronuclei and failed-cytokinesis morphology (Aurora signature, e4), and the hard measurements agree — frac_large_nucleus strongly up (z +9 to +17 across doses, e2/e3/e7/e8), multinucleate proxy up, nuclear solidity/form-factor collapsing, while frac_mitotic_like stays at ~0 at every dose (z -0.6 to 0). Eg5 inhibition should produce mitotic/monopolar arrest with an elevated mitotic-like fraction; its complete absence is barely weighed against the atlas vote, which may simply reflect shared mitotic-failure morphology. The flip from 0.50 to 0.68 for Eg5 on the basis of re-running the same NSC over more same-replicate (all rep 1) wells is overconfident, and the key discriminating observation (polyploidy without mitotic arrest) rests on a single 1 uM visual read.
